Photograph: Oliver Contreras/AFP/Getty Images US news Republican holdouts say they will back Todd Blanche for attorney general Move comes after Blanche gives senators written assurance he will drop Trump’s $1.8bn anti-weaponization fund Shrai Popat and Guardian staff in Washington Mon 3 Aug 2026 14.01 EDT First published on Mon 3 Aug 2026 11.51 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Two Republican senators who threatened to block Todd Blanche’s bid to permanently become US attorney general announced they will advance his nomination after he said in writing that a planned $1.8bn slush fund for Donald Trump’s allies was dead. The US Senate judiciary committee is due to vote on Tuesday on whether to approve the nomination of Blanche, who is already acting attorney general, and send it to the wider Senate for a vote. Outgoing lawmakers John Cornyn and Thom Tillis, two key holdouts on the committee who have repeatedly clashed with Trump over the past year, said their concerns were resolved after a “successful negotiation of a legally enforceable document”, which was released by Blanche late on Sunday. Blanche formally rescinds Trump’s $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponization fund’ ahead of nomination hearing Read more The document formally ends the $1.8bn “anti‑weaponization fund”, and makes clear that Trump and his family will not receive indefinite protection from audits of future tax filings. Both controversial prospects arose from an agreement reached as part of a settlement in a lawsuit Trump filed against the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) over the unauthorized leak of his tax returns. A US federal judge who oversaw the lawsuit blasted the arrangement, noting that the US Department of Justice did not make a good faith effort to defend the government, and that it appeared to be a collusive effort to engineer a beneficial result on behalf of the president. Both the fund and the scope of Trump’s immunity from tax audits became dealbreakers for Cornyn and Tillis. “We are pleased that the Department of Justice has issued a formal order terminating the anti-weaponization fund,” the senators said in a joint statement. “Additionally, the department has acknowledged in a binding written order that the audit settlement is limited to the plaintiffs and the scope does not extend beyond the defendants in the lawsuit, the IRS and the Treasury, addressing concerns that multiple of our Republican colleagues share. “We look forward to voting to advance his nomination out of the Senate judiciary committee soon.” Just this weekend, Trump had defended the fund, and threatened to “push hard” to legislate for it. The fund would “immediately be back on the table, and I will get it done” if senators fail to approve Blanche’s nomination, the president wrote on social media. https://www.baltictimes.com/seimas_speak.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Seimas speaker says Zemaitaitis impeachment should await final ruling 2026-07-22 BNS/TBT Staff VILNIUS - Lithuania's parliament speaker Juozas Olekas said on Wednesday that impeachment proceedings against opposition Nemunas Dawn leader Remigijus Zemaitaitis should wait until the deadline for an appeal expires or the Supreme Court issues a final ruling. "Impeachment is initiated once a final decision is in force, either from the Supreme Court or if the Court of Appeal ruling is not contested through cassation," the speaker told reporters. "We must wait for either the appeal period to pass or for the Supreme Court's decision." However, Olekas did not rule out the possibility of lawmakers gathering the necessary signatures to propose starting the impeachment process sooner. Zemaitaitis' fate will likely be decided in the autumn, the speaker said. On Wednesday, the Lithuanian Court of Appeal found Zemaitaitis guilty of inciting hatred against Jews and grossly trivialising the Holocaust, increasing his fine from 5,000 to 10,000 euros. The court ruled that the politician's public statements about Jews crossed the boundaries of lawful freedom of expression, systematically mocking, disparaging and promoting hatred against people of Jewish nationality. The ruling took effect immediately but can be appealed. Zemaitaitis has pledged to challenge the verdict. The criminal case stems from Facebook posts and public remarks made in May and June 2023. In the posts, he referred to Israelis as "animals" and claimed that Jews contributed to the destruction of the Lithuanian nation. Impeachment proceedings were previously initiated against the politician over the posts. In April 2024, the Constitutional Court ruled that he had broken his oath and committed a gross violation of the Constitution. Following that ruling, Zemaitaitis resigned his seat in the Seimas but was re-elected to parliament in the autumn of 2024. The speaker suggested that consideration should be given to preventing situations in which a politician can avoid the consequences of impeachment by resigning and then running for office again. He said proposals for such procedural changes could be prepared by the autumn session of the Seimas. Olekas also emphasised that the Lithuanian state's position on anti-Semitism and hatred was clear, and that statements by individual members of parliament did not reflect official state policy. https://baltic-review.com/paide-opinion-.text: Share Tweet 0 Paide’s Castle Hill hosts the 2026 Opinion Festival from August 7 to 8. Paide’s historic Castle Hill becomes the centre of Estonia’s civic and cultural life on Friday, August 7, as the 2026 Opinion Festival opens for a two-day programme of public discussions, workshops and community activities. The festival continues through Saturday, August 8, offering an open setting for people to listen, ask questions and exchange ideas on issues connected with everyday life and Estonia’s future. The event is one of the country’s best-established discussion festivals. Organisers describe it as Estonia’s largest platform for public debate, while the municipality of Paide identifies it as a major annual event for the town and the wider Järva region. The 2026 festival is being held under the broad theme of dialogue: the organisers emphasise the ability and willingness to address differences through conversation rather than confrontation. ([arvamusfestival.ee](https://arvamusfestival.ee/?utm_source=openai)) A public meeting place in a small town Unlike a conventional conference held in a single auditorium, the Opinion Festival spreads across Paide Castle Hill and its surrounding areas. Visitors move between discussion spaces, outdoor stages and activity zones, creating a format that combines public affairs with the atmosphere of a summer town festival. The programme is designed for a wide audience rather than a specialist professional group. The official festival description lists entrepreneurs, politicians, researchers, civil-society representatives, cultural figures and members of the public among those who meet in Paide. The event’s organisers say that more than 9,000 people gather over the two festival days, making the occasion significant both as a national meeting point and as a local cultural event. ([arvamusfestival.ee](https://arvamusfestival.ee/?utm_source=openai)) Discussion areas address themes including education, climate, technology, culture and ordinary community life. The range is intentional: the festival treats civic culture not only as a matter for elected officials or academic experts, but also as something shaped by families, local organisations, businesses and visitors willing to take part. Dialogue beyond the discussion stages The 2026 programme also includes music, poetry, workshops, children’s activities and informal meeting areas. These elements give the festival a more relaxed character and help connect structured debate with the social habits of a town centre: walking, stopping, listening and encountering people with different experiences. For Paide, the festival has become part of the city’s identity. The municipality has described the event as a civic initiative supported by volunteers, partners and local government. Paide’s role is not simply to host a temporary programme; the town presents itself as a meeting place where national conversations can take place in a smaller and more accessible setting than the capital. The festival is also open to young visitors. Estonia’s national youth information portal Teeviit lists the event as a free public festival in Paide and presents it as a place where people can listen, think, ask questions and participate in conversations about society. ([teeviit.ee](https://www.teeviit.ee/sundmus/arvamusfestival/?utm_source=openai)) Why the event matters culturally Public discussion festivals occupy an unusual space between culture, education and civic life. They do not produce a single performance or exhibition, yet they create a shared cultural experience through conversation. Their value lies partly in the setting: a historic landscape becomes a temporary public room where ideas are presented alongside music, food, children’s programming and the rhythms of a summer weekend. That combination is particularly visible in Paide. The town’s compact centre allows the festival to remain walkable, while Castle Hill provides a distinctive historical backdrop. Visitors can therefore experience the event both as a programme of discussions and as a way of exploring one of Estonia’s smaller regional centres. The organisers’ emphasis on listening and constructive exchange also gives the 2026 edition a clear public purpose. The festival does not require visitors to arrive with a fixed position. Instead, its format encourages them to compare viewpoints, learn from participants and discover subjects outside their usual interests. A weekend invitation to Paide With the programme now public and the event opening on August 7, the Opinion Festival offers a timely cultural destination for the second weekend of August. Its appeal is broad: visitors may come for a particular discussion, a workshop, the children’s area, the cultural programme or simply the atmosphere of a town temporarily organised around ideas. In a country where cultural life often extends beyond traditional concert halls and museums, Paide’s festival demonstrates how public conversation can itself become a form of cultural participation. For two days, the town invites Estonia to slow down, meet in person and consider how shared ideas are formed. https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/09/11/outdo.text: Outdoor cinema screenings continue in the old town of Nicosia as To Erma presents three more evenings of films in its courtyard. Amid its wooden chairs, colourful plant pots and trees, this bookstore brings back its summer cinema evenings to the heart of town. Three events have been added to September’s agenda, every Monday until the end of the month. All film screenings start at 8pm and have free admission. Organisers advise movie-goers to reserve their spot, however, as spaces are limited. Works from European cinema, American comedy and contemporary cinema are on the programme. The next screening, on September 14, is Millions, a 2004 film by Danny Boyle about two brothers who discover a suitcase full of money shortly before the euro is introduced. The older brother wants to spend it on consumer goods, while the younger, who has visions of saints, wants to give it to the poor. Hungarian film Comrade Draculich follows next, on September 21, set in 1970s Hungary. Fabian, a hero of the Cuban Revolution, arrives in the country to promote a blood donation campaign for Vietnam. But something strange is going on with the veteran comrade: he looks like he’s in his thirties, is effortlessly cool and drives a magnificent Mustang. A young secret police couple is assigned to keep tabs on him. The final film of the series on September 28 is What Just Happened, an American film starring Robert De Niro, John Turturro, Stanley Tucci, Sean Penn, Catherine Keener, Bruce Willis, Robin Wright and Kristen Stewart. It follows the life of a Hollywood producer who struggles to cope with a tough studio boss, a director who refuses to re-edit his film, a neurotic agent, a difficult star and his ex-wife, with whom he wants to rekindle their relationship. Summer Cinema – To Erma Screening of 2004 UK film Millions. September 14. Screening of Comrade Draculich. September 21. What Just Happened. September 28. To Erma, Nicosia. 8pm. Free admission. Reservations required. Tel: 22-346770
